topic: GitHub Copilot Code Review: Agent Skills and MCP Now Generally Available

key_points: Copilot code review support for agent skills and MCP servers is now GA for all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise users
Agent skills let Copilot code review invoke team's internal tools and coding standards during review via SKILL.md files under .github/skills/
MCP server connections pull context from third-party platforms (issue trackers, docs, service catalogs) directly into review
All MCP tool calls by Copilot code review are limited to read-only
GitHub and Playwright MCP servers are turned on by default
New attribution on skills and MCP comments shows which skill/MCP server generated each comment
Existing MCP configs for Copilot cloud agent automatically apply to code review
Copilot code review runs on agentic tool-calling architecture using GitHub Actions runners
Starting June 1, 2026, each Copilot code review consumes GitHub Actions minutes from plan entitlement
Billed in two ways: AI Credits (usage-based billing) + GitHub Actions minutes for private repos
Supports self-hosted runners and larger GitHub-hosted runners at different rates
Public repositories remain free for Actions minutes
Copilot code review first reached GA in April 2025
Over 1 million developers used it within the first month of public preview
Helps offload basic reviews to find bugs, performance problems, and suggest fixes
Available to all paid Copilot subscribers
Supports C, C++, Kotlin, Swift, HTML, and txt
Copilot code review can be requested from GitHub CLI
Enables CLI-based PR review workflows without leaving terminal
Portable agent skills collection for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot
Markdown-only skills with no runtime dependencies
Includes code review, vertical-slice architecture, Go testing, low cognitive-complexity enforcement
Installable via npx skills
38 portable agent skills for disciplined, reviewable AI-assisted work
Works across Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and compatible agents
Includes workflow, feature-planning, testing skills
Installable via npx skills or apm
Easy-to-use, high-quality secure code review agent skills
CWE-based code review with structured kill chain reasoning
Supports Markdown and JSON output formats
Works with lower-end and higher-end LLMs

stats.fact: Over 1 million developers used Copilot code review within the first month of its public preview (April 2025)
Copilot code review is now available to all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise subscribers
Starting June 1, 2026, Copilot code review consumes GitHub Actions minutes for private repositories
GitHub Copilot transitioned to usage-based billing (AI Credits) on June 1, 2026, replacing premium request units (PRUs)
Copilot Pro ($10/mo) includes $10 in monthly AI Credits; Business ($19/user/mo) includes $19; Enterprise ($39/user/mo) includes $39
Adaptive Skills offers 38 portable agent skills for AI-assisted work across multiple coding agents
MCP tool calls by Copilot code review are limited to read-only operations
GitHub and Playwright MCP servers are enabled by default for Copilot code review

angles: Agent skills and MCP transform Copilot code review from a static linter into a context-aware reviewer that understands team conventions and external systems
The read-only MCP constraint balances power with safety — Copilot can read from issue trackers and docs but cannot mutate external systems during review
Attribution on comments (showing which skill/MCP generated each comment) increases transparency and trust in AI-generated code review feedback
The ecosystem of portable agent skills (mryll/skills, adaptive-skills, secure-code-review) creates a marketplace effect where teams can share and reuse review expertise
Usage-based billing (AI Credits + Actions minutes) means teams need to optimize their review workflows to control costs
Agent skills can be targeted specifically to code review via review-focused skill directory names, enabling specialized review personas
